question: If knowledge is truly described, why would things stay unknowable?
premises: even true description leaves them unknowable
as with the broad-based pot, real yet ungrasped
truth of description does not yield grasp
inference: Description-truth and knowability come apart; the pot proves it.
uncertainties: prthubudhna pot-example kept as stated, деталей not pressed
plain_english: They would indeed be unknowable even when knowledge is truly described — as with the pot of broad-based form, even though it is real.
